identity.title: Sequences of Logits Reveal the Low Rank Structure of Language Models

problem.claim: Understanding the inherent low-dimensional structure of large language models.

contributions.claim: Introduces a model-agnostic approach that studies language models as sequential probabilistic models.
Reports approximate low-rank structure in logit-derived matrices across a wide range of modern language models.
Uses the low-rank structure for response generation and develops a universal abstraction with provable learning guarantees.

stated_novelty.claim: The proposed perspective is model-agnostic and treats language models as sequential probabilistic models, yielding a simple universal abstraction for approximate-rank analysis.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that matrices constructed from logits over varying prompts and responses have low approximate rank across a wide range of modern language models.
The authors report generating a target-prompt response from a linear combination of outputs on unrelated or nonsensical prompts.
The authors report provable learning guarantees for their abstraction.

narrative_sequence.summary: Frames understanding language models' inherent low-dimensional structure as a major problem.
Reports approximate low rank in logit matrices across modern models.
Shows that the structure can support generation from outputs on unrelated or nonsensical prompts.
Presents a universal abstraction whose predictions parallel the experiments and analyzes its representation power with learning guarantees.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects an empirical structural observation—approximate low rank—to a concrete generation procedure and then to a theoretical abstraction with guarantees.

lessons.interpretation: A structural claim becomes more informative when the paper traces both an operational consequence and a formal explanatory model.
lessons.application: When presenting a discovered model property, pair it with a task-level use and a deliberately simplified abstraction whose predictions can be compared with observations.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the structural measurement has no clear downstream operation or when formalization would obscure essential task-specific behavior.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluated models, prompt and response sets, rank criteria, or quantitative results.
The generation procedure, linear-combination construction, and its conditions are unspecified.
The assumptions and scope of the provable learning guarantees are not given.
